name: Calm lo-fi bed
line: A soft, warm lo-fi beat sits low under the voice and never hurries.

prompt.what: A warm lo-fi bed at its own 92.9 bpm, with picture changes on bar starts, one bar apart, every 2.58 s. The music dips 12 dB under each spoken line and comes back up in the gaps, and about 14% of the film rests on the bed alone with no new sound.
prompt.when: Fits quiet explainers, onboarding and how-to films where the voice leads and nothing should feel rushed.
prompt.avoid: Cutting on single beats, because this beat drifts a little, so cut on bar starts and check by ear; and hard hits or booms, which the bed cannot carry.

name: Steady pulse for demos
line: A clean electronic pulse that keeps time under a product walk-through without ever building.

prompt.what: A clean, even electronic pulse at 120 bpm that never builds or drops, so each demo step lands on a bar start, one every 2 s. It dips 9 dB under each spoken line and can be trimmed or looped at any bar without a seam.
prompt.when: Fits product demos, feature tours and walk-throughs where the screen is the show and the music only keeps time.
prompt.avoid: Asking it to carry a big reveal, since it has no peak; add a riser or a sting for the payoff instead.

name: Driving electronic, flat out
line: Fast electronic drums at full drive from the first frame, for an ad that never lets up.

prompt.what: Start the driving track in its loudest stretch, 38.6 s in, so the film runs at full drive from frame one at 143.1 bpm; cut every two beats, 0.84 s, and slam each word on a downbeat. Under a voice it dips only 6 dB, so keep lines short, and rest the sound no more than 5% of the film.
prompt.when: Fits launch ads, hype reels and sports-energy cuts for vertical feeds.
prompt.avoid: Long voice lines and calm products, and an even cut on every beat, which turns into a metronome; vary between one and four beats.

name: Electronic track that climbs
line: The music starts lean and steps up twice, so the film gets bigger as the story does.

prompt.what: Play the driving track from its start so it climbs in two steps, at 25.2 s and 38.6 s, and set the film's turns on them: the problem on the lean opening, the product on the first step, proof and offer on the full stretch. Cut once a bar, 1.68 s, before the second step, then every two beats, 0.84 s, after it, all at 143.1 bpm; lines dip the music 9 dB before the second step and 6 dB after it.
prompt.when: Fits launch films of 40 to 55 s that should open measured and finish at full energy.
prompt.avoid: Films under 30 s, which never reach the steps, and spending the main reveal before 25 s.

name: Quiet build, reveal on the drop
line: The music builds quietly, then drops to full energy at the exact moment the product appears.

prompt.what: Build the film over the track's quiet opening and put the product reveal exactly on its drop, 24.0 s in; for a shorter film start the track on a bar 14.4 s in, so the drop lands 9.6 s into the film. Cut once a bar, 2.4 s, at 100.1 bpm before the drop, and every two beats, 1.2 s, after it in a hype film, with lines dipping the music 9 dB (6 dB at hype).
prompt.when: Fits reveals and launches where one moment matters most and the viewer should feel it coming.
prompt.avoid: Spending the drop on a logo or a title nobody reads; land the product doing its main job there.

name: Start on the drop
line: The music is already at full energy on the first frame, with no build at all.

prompt.what: Begin the music on its drop, 24.0 s into the build and drop track, so the first frame already plays at full energy at 100.1 bpm; cut every two beats, 1.2 s, and on every beat, 0.6 s, through the 2 s hook. Rest the sound no more than 5% of the film, and dip it 6 dB under any line.
prompt.when: Fits paid social ads of 6 to 15 s that cannot spend time building.
prompt.avoid: A calm voice-over on top, and a riser at the start, since there is nothing left to build to.

name: Tension build, no release
line: Only the rising part of the track plays, and the film ends before the music lets go.

prompt.what: Use only the build and drop track's rising first 21 s and end the film on a held bar before the drop ever comes, so the viewer is left leaning in. Cut once a bar, 2.4 s, at 100.1 bpm, and let the last bar ring under the title instead of cutting it; lines dip it 9 dB.
prompt.when: Fits teasers and announcements that should end on a question rather than an answer.
prompt.avoid: Letting the drop in, and teasers longer than about 22 s, which run out of build.

name: Upbeat groove
line: A warm, bright groove that is busy from the first bar and keeps smiling.

prompt.what: A warm, bright groove at 120 bpm that is busy from its first bar; cut once a bar, 2 s, in a confident film or every two beats, 1 s, at hype, with numbers and the logo on bar starts. Its full stretch lasts 40 s, so a film up to that length never sags; it dips 9 dB under a line (6 dB at hype).
prompt.when: Fits feature announcements, customer stories and upbeat social films.
prompt.avoid: Serious or sensitive subjects, and long voice-overs fighting its busy middle.

name: Playful chiptune
line: Light, bouncy video-game music for a friendly film that does not take itself too seriously.

prompt.what: Light pixel-game music at 120 bpm; cut every two beats, 1 s, and give small elements a soft pop on the beat between cuts. It dips 9 dB under a line, and its bright top end stays clear of the voice.
prompt.when: Fits friendly product films, apps with a playful brand and social cut-downs.
prompt.avoid: Premium, finance and health brands, and heavy booms that clash with its toy-like sound.

name: Solo piano, reflective
line: One piano playing slow, open chords, for a film that should feel honest and still.

prompt.what: A new piano piece at 84 bpm, mostly sustained chords with a simple top line, changing chord with the picture once a bar, every 2.86 s. It sits 12 dB under the voice and leaves 15% of the film to single held notes.
prompt.when: Fits founder notes, mission films and thank-you messages where warmth matters more than drive.
prompt.avoid: Busy runs under the voice, and sad minor keys that turn a product film into a eulogy.

name: Acoustic guitar and claps
line: Strummed steel-string guitar, foot stomps and hand claps, earthy, like a band on a porch.

prompt.what: A new full-band acoustic piece at 104 bpm: strummed steel-string guitar, a stomp on every beat and claps on two and four, and a chorus that lifts with a second guitar; cut once a bar, 2.31 s, and let the claps drop out for one bar before the payoff. It dips 9 dB under each line.
prompt.when: Fits small businesses, food, travel and maker brands that want to feel handmade.
prompt.avoid: Tech launches that should feel precise, and a whistled hook, which wears out fast.

name: Orchestral swell
line: Strings, brass and big drums rising to one huge moment, like a film trailer.

prompt.what: A new orchestral cue at 100 bpm (120 at hype): low strings and a pulse for the set-up, brass entering a bar before the peak, and full drums on the reveal. Cut once a bar, 2.4 s, while it builds and every two beats, 1 s, at hype, with one bar of near silence before the biggest hit; lines dip it 9 dB (6 dB at hype).
prompt.when: Fits big launches, keynote openers and brand films that should feel cinematic.
prompt.avoid: Small everyday products, where it sounds like a joke, and stacking choir on top, which buries the voice.

name: Ambient pads, no beat
line: Soft, slowly shifting synth chords with no drums, like a calm room of light.

prompt.what: New soft pads with no drums, each chord swelling in over about a bar at a slow count of 80 bpm, so a picture change every 3 s rides a swell. The pads sit 12 dB under the voice and 15% of the film is held with nothing new.
prompt.when: Fits wellness, calm technology and data films that need space more than rhythm.
prompt.avoid: Fast cuts, which have no beat to land on, and long films over 60 s, where pads alone feel empty.

name: Head-nod hip-hop beat
line: A dusty drum loop with a deep bass line that makes heads nod.

prompt.what: A new hip-hop loop at 100 bpm with a heavy kick, a crisp snare on two and four and a round bass line; cut once a bar, 2.4 s, and drop the drums for half a bar under the key line. It dips 9 dB under the voice.
prompt.when: Fits street, fashion, creator and youth brands with a confident voice.
prompt.avoid: Vocal samples or scratches that sound like a known record, and corporate subjects.

name: Hard trap with deep bass
line: Rolling hi-hats over a booming bass, for a bold, swaggering ad.

prompt.what: A new trap beat at 130 bpm with half-time drums, rolling hi-hats and a long, booming bass note on each drop; cut every two beats, 0.92 s, and land word slams on the bass hits. Under a voice it dips 6 dB.
prompt.when: Fits sneaker, gaming, drinks and creator-brand ads for vertical feeds.
prompt.avoid: Phone-speaker-only mixes where the bass vanishes; check that the hits still read on a small speaker.

name: Funk and disco
line: Slap bass, bright guitar chops and a kick on every beat that feels like a party.

prompt.what: A new funk piece at 116 bpm (124 at hype) with a kick on every beat, chopped guitar and a busy bass; cut once a bar, 2.07 s, or every two beats, 0.97 s, at hype, and stop the band dead for one beat before the offer; lines dip it 9 dB (6 dB at hype).
prompt.when: Fits fashion, food, events and seasonal sales with a fun streak.
prompt.avoid: Serious B2B subjects, and long voice lines over the busy bass.

name: Retro synthwave
line: Eighties synths and a gated drum beat, glossy and a little nostalgic.

prompt.what: A new synthwave track at 110 bpm with an arpeggio, a warm bass and a big gated snare on two and four; cut once a bar, 2.18 s, and open a new synth layer every four bars so long films keep moving; it dips 9 dB under each line.
prompt.when: Fits gaming, creative tools, night-time and retro-styled brands.
prompt.avoid: Brands that should feel modern and plain, where it reads as a costume.

name: Drums only, no melody
line: Just drums, claps and shakers, leaving every note of space for the voice.

prompt.what: A new percussion bed at 112 bpm (126 at hype) with no chords at all, so it never clashes with a brand sting; cut once a bar, 2.14 s, or every two beats, 0.95 s, at hype, and add one layer of percussion per section; lines dip it 9 dB (6 dB at hype).
prompt.when: Fits films with a lot of voice, or a brand sting that should own the melody.
prompt.avoid: Films over 45 s, where drums alone tire the ear without a change.

name: Café jazz with brushes
line: Upright bass, soft piano and brushed drums, relaxed and grown-up.

prompt.what: A new light jazz trio at 96 bpm with brushed drums, walking bass and sparse piano; picture changes fall on bar starts, every 2.5 s, and the piano rests while the voice speaks, with the band 12 dB under it.
prompt.when: Fits hospitality, finance, books and premium services that want to feel unhurried and confident.
prompt.avoid: Busy piano solos under lines, and quick cuts that fight the swing.

name: Festival dance anthem
line: A big dance track with a kick on every beat, a long build and a stadium drop.

prompt.what: A new dance track at 128 bpm with an eight-bar build, a beat of silence, then the drop; cut every two beats, 0.94 s, after the drop and put the product on the first kick back. Under a voice it dips 6 dB.
prompt.when: Fits events, launches with a party feel and recap films of a big day.
prompt.avoid: Voice-led films, and drops that arrive before the viewer knows what the film is about.

name: Sunny ukulele
line: A small, toy-like tune of plucked ukulele and glockenspiel with finger snaps and no drums.

prompt.what: A new light piece at 108 bpm with no drums at all: plucked ukulele, a glockenspiel tune and soft finger snaps on two and four; cut once a bar, 2.22 s, and let the glockenspiel answer each on-screen tick with one note; it dips 9 dB under each line.
prompt.when: Fits family, pet, kids and everyday-app films that should feel kind and easy.
prompt.avoid: Anything premium or technical, and running it longer than 30 s, where its cheer wears thin.

name: Ticking tension
line: A low pulse and a ticking clock that make the problem feel urgent.

prompt.what: A new low pulse at 104 bpm with a tick on every beat and a bass note each bar, every 2.31 s, under the problem part of the film; at the turn it stops dead for half a second and the brighter music takes over; it dips 9 dB under each line.
prompt.when: Fits ads that show a problem before the fix, deadlines, security and money-saving films.
prompt.avoid: Running it under the product itself, which makes the product feel like the threat.

name: Quiet dry clicks
line: Every click and key gets a tiny, dry tick you feel more than hear.

prompt.what: Give every press, key and toggle one dry, nearly silent tick on the exact frame the pointer lands, and one airy whoosh that starts 0.15 s before each scene change. Accents come about once a bar, every 2.67 s on a 90 bpm cut (2.18 s at 110 bpm when confident), and effects dip 12 dB under each spoken line (9 dB when confident).
prompt.when: Fits software and productivity demos that should feel calm, precise and expensive.
prompt.avoid: Sounds for actions the viewer cannot see, and two ticks closer than 0.3 s, which read as a stutter.

name: Glass and crystal
line: Bright, glassy taps and a crystal chime when something succeeds.

prompt.what: Clicks are crystalline taps, switches rise when they turn on and fall when they turn off, and the result lands on one glass success chime timed so its first ring meets the tick or number on screen. Taps fall about once a bar, every 2.18 s at 110 bpm (2.67 s at 90 bpm when calm), with effects dipping 9 dB under each line (12 dB when calm).
prompt.when: Fits premium software, finance and design tools that want a polished, high-end feel.
prompt.avoid: Using the success chime more than twice in a film, and pairing it with heavy booms.

name: Wood and warm stone
line: Dry wooden taps and soft knocks, like objects set down on a table.

prompt.what: Presses become dry wooden taps, items arrive with a small pebble-like pop, and a finished task gets one short wooden chime. Sounds fall about once a bar, every 2.67 s at 90 bpm, sit 12 dB under each spoken line, and 14% of the film rests with no effect at all.
prompt.when: Fits wellness, food, craft, education and calm lifestyle apps.
prompt.avoid: Tech films that should feel digital, and laying it over a fast beat.

name: Firm mechanical switches
line: Solid switch clicks and hard key strikes, like real hardware.

prompt.what: Every press is a firm switch with its own release 0.08 s later, keys strike hard, deletes land with a mechanical thunk, and fast whooshes carry the cuts. Accents can come every two beats, 1.09 s at 110 bpm or 0.94 s at 128 bpm when hype, and effects dip only 8 dB under a line (6 dB at hype).
prompt.when: Fits developer tools, hardware, keyboards, gaming gear and engineering products.
prompt.avoid: Calm consumer apps, and a click on every letter of long typing, which chatters.

name: Rubbery, bouncy taps
line: Soft, elastic taps and pops that make the interface feel friendly and squishy.

prompt.what: Taps are soft and elastic, new elements pop in with a rubbery boing timed to the top of their bounce, and confirms end with a small upward lift. Accents fall about once a bar, every 2.18 s at 110 bpm, and dip 9 dB under each spoken line.
prompt.when: Fits consumer apps, games, kids and playful brands with springy animation.
prompt.avoid: Serious subjects, and stiff animation with no bounce, where the sound has nothing to match.

name: Pixel arcade blips
line: Cheerful video-game blips for every tap, and a level-up sound for the win.

prompt.what: Taps and pops are bright pixel blips, a question on screen gets a little rising blip, and the result plays a level-up run timed so its last note meets the payoff. Blips can come every two beats, 1 s at 120 bpm (0.94 s at 128 bpm when hype), dipping 8 dB under a line (6 dB at hype).
prompt.when: Fits games, quizzes, rewards, learning apps and anything with points or streaks.
prompt.avoid: Premium and B2B brands, and real-world footage, where the blips feel pasted on.

name: Phone in the hand
line: Fingertip taps and swipes on glass, and a phone buzzing on the table.

prompt.what: Every touch is a soft fingertip tap on glass on the frame of contact, swipes get a short swish of skin on glass lasting as long as the gesture, and alerts are a real phone buzzing on a table. Touches fall about once a bar, every 2.67 s at 90 bpm calm or 2.18 s at 110 bpm confident, and dip 12 dB (calm) or 9 dB (confident) under each line.
prompt.when: Fits mobile app demos, phone-framed films and social clips shot on a phone.
prompt.avoid: Mouse clicks inside a phone film, and the table buzz when no phone is on screen.

name: Typing on a laptop
line: Real laptop typing under every field that fills, ending on a soft send.

prompt.what: When a field fills, the first word gets one key sound per letter, then a real laptop typing run carries the rest and stops on the frame the last letter appears, followed by a soft send. Typing moments come about once a bar or less, every 2.67 s at 90 bpm (2.18 s at 110 bpm when confident), 12 dB under a spoken line (9 dB when confident).
prompt.when: Fits AI prompt films, writing tools, search and chat products where typing is the action.
prompt.avoid: Typing sound running on after the text has stopped, and a key sound for every letter of a long line.

name: Paper and cards on a desk
line: Cards sliding, pages turning and a pen clicking, like working at a real desk.

prompt.what: Cards slide in with a soft paper drag and land with a light tap, pages flip between sections, and a pen click marks the moment something is signed or ticked. Sounds fall about once a bar, every 2.67 s at 90 bpm, sit 12 dB under each line, and 14% of the film is quiet.
prompt.when: Fits paper-look films, planning, legal, education and editorial explainers.
prompt.avoid: Screen recordings with no paper on screen, and mixing it with digital blips.

name: Chat and messages
line: Messages send with a lift and arrive with a clean ping, like a busy chat app.

prompt.what: Each sent message gets a short rising send on the frame the bubble leaves, each reply a clean digital ping as it appears, and typing dots a tiny tick. Messages come about once a bar, every 2.18 s at 110 bpm, and every sound dips 9 dB under a spoken line.
prompt.when: Fits messaging, support, AI assistant and team chat products.
prompt.avoid: A ping on every message in a fast scroll; sound only the ones the viewer reads.

name: Ticking numbers and panels
line: Numbers tick as they count up and panels open with a small rising tone.

prompt.what: Counting numbers get a fine run of ticks that stops on the frame the number settles, panels open with a short rising tone and close with a falling one, and each new chart point plucks softly. Panel moves land about once a bar, every 2.18 s at 110 bpm, 9 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits dashboards, analytics, finance and reporting films.
prompt.avoid: Ticks that keep running after the number has landed, and a sound for every point of a dense chart.

name: Real mouse clicks
line: Honest plastic mouse clicks, press and release, as if someone is at the desk.

prompt.what: Each click is split into a press on the frame the pointer lands and a release 0.08 s later, menus open and close with soft puffs, and hovering over a control gives a barely-there tick. Clicks fall about once a bar, every 2.67 s at 90 bpm calm or 2.18 s at 110 bpm confident, 12 dB (calm) or 9 dB (confident) under the voice.
prompt.when: Fits tutorials and screen-recorded walk-throughs where the viewer copies each step.
prompt.avoid: Hover ticks on every pass of the pointer, and clicks in a film with no visible pointer.

name: Bubble-wrap pops
line: Snappy plastic pops as each item, sticker or word lands, quick as popping bubble wrap.

prompt.what: Every list item, sticker or caption word lands with a snappy pop, one per beat at 128 bpm, 0.47 s apart, switching between real bubble pops and bubble-wrap pops so no two in a row sound the same. A quick hand swish carries each cut, and effects dip 6 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits creator-style lists, top-five films, product hauls and fast social cuts.
prompt.avoid: More than about eight pops in a row without a rest, and calm or premium brands.

name: Soft, dreamy blooms
line: Things appear with a soft airy bloom, and a task ends on a gentle shimmer.

prompt.what: New elements fade in on a soft bloom that swells over about 0.3 s so its peak meets the element's full size, airy whooshes carry the slow cuts, and a finished task gets one gentle shimmer. Blooms come about once a bar, every 2.67 s at 90 bpm, 12 dB under each line, with 15% of the film left quiet.
prompt.when: Fits sleep, wellness, journaling and calm creative apps.
prompt.avoid: Fast cuts and hard hits, and using the shimmer for anything but the one real result.

name: Pro studio presses
line: Warm, tactile presses like the buttons on studio gear, for creative tools.

prompt.what: Presses are warm and tactile with a little body, sends rise briefly, switches click with a short dry snap and timeline scrubs get a soft run of detents. Presses fall about once a bar, every 2.18 s at 110 bpm, and every sound dips 9 dB under a spoken line.
prompt.when: Fits editors, music, photo and design software aimed at professionals.
prompt.avoid: Cartoon pops, and stacking more than two sounds on one action.

name: Punches and whips
line: Hard punches on the key words and whip swishes on the cuts, for a loud, fast ad.

prompt.what: Key words slam in on a hard punch on their exact landing frame, at most one punch a bar, 1.88 s at 128 bpm, while whip swishes peaking on each cut carry the shots between. Effects dip only 6 dB under a line, and no more than 5% of the film is without sound.
prompt.when: Fits paid social, sports, fitness and launch ads built on word slams.
prompt.avoid: A punch on every word, which numbs the ear; save them for the words that sell.

name: Trailer weight
line: Deep booms, rumbling whooshes and a long build, like a cinema trailer.

prompt.what: Big moments land on a deep boom on the exact frame, scene changes rush past on a heavy dark whoosh, and a long build runs under the opening. Booms are rare, one every two bars at most, 4 s at 120 bpm, and effects dip 6 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits big launches, keynote openers, games and title sequences.
prompt.avoid: Calm films and small talking-head edits, and a boom on more than three moments in a film.

name: Errors, then the fix
line: Buzzy errors and cancels in the "before" half, clean confirms once the product fixes it.

prompt.what: In the before half, each failure gets a short two-tone error buzz and things thrown away fall with a dark delete; from the turn on, the same actions land on clean rising confirms. The switch happens on one frame at the turn, accents fall about once a bar, every 2.18 s at 110 bpm, and effects dip 9 dB under each line.
prompt.when: Fits ads that show the problem before the fix, before and after films and switching stories.
prompt.avoid: Harsh error sounds repeated more than three times, which make the film itself feel broken.

name: Fabric, zips and leather
line: Cloth rustles, zips and a soft leather set-down, for products you hold or wear.

prompt.what: Bags open on a real zip lasting as long as the pull, fabric rustles as things move or turn, and a soft leather set-down lands on the frame an object touches the surface. Sounds fall about once a bar, every 2.67 s at 90 bpm calm or 2.18 s at 110 bpm confident, 12 dB (calm) or 9 dB (confident) under a line.
prompt.when: Fits fashion, bags, outdoor gear and any physical product filmed or modelled close up.
prompt.avoid: Screen-only films, and a zip sound when the zip is out of frame.

name: Voice alone on room tone
line: No music at all: just the voice over the quiet sound of a clean room.

prompt.what: No music; the voice sits alone over clean room tone, a soft bed of air with no hum, kept at one level so it never dips (0 dB) and no cut ever drops to dead silence. Cuts follow the voice's phrases on a slow count of 84 bpm, about every 2.86 s (2.4 s at 100 bpm when confident), and 14% of a calm film holds on a breath with only the room.
prompt.when: Fits talking heads, founder messages, tutorials and honest customer stories where music would feel like selling.
prompt.avoid: Real silence between lines, which sounds broken, and adding music under only part of the film.

name: Rain outside, then shelter
line: Open rain fills the problem part, then turns to the cosy patter of rain on a roof once the product arrives.

prompt.what: No music; wide, open rain plays under the problem, then crossfades over 1 s at the turn into close rain drumming on a roof, so the product feels like shelter. Both dip 10 dB under each line and rise back over 0.45 s in the gaps; cuts ride a slow count of 84 bpm, about every 2.86 s, and 15% of the film is left to the rain alone.
prompt.when: Fits cosy products, home, insurance, coffee and books, where the product is the shelter from a grey day.
prompt.avoid: Bright, sunny pictures, and stacking music on top, which turns the rain into hiss.

name: Sea air, no music
line: Waves on a beach set the pace: each new shot arrives as a wave breaks.

prompt.what: Waves on a beach replace the music, with the biggest picture changes placed on a wave breaking and the rest on a slow count of 80 bpm, about every 3 s. The waves dip 10 dB under each line and 15% of the film rests on the sea alone.
prompt.when: Fits travel, summer, wellness and outdoor brands, and calm product reveals.
prompt.avoid: Indoor or screen-only films, where the sea has no reason to be there.

name: Forest morning
line: The film opens on a quiet forest alone before anyone speaks, and closes on it again.

prompt.what: No music; the film opens on the forest alone for 2 s before the first word, sinks 10 dB under the voice, and rises back to full for the last 2 s after the final line. Picture changes ride a slow count of 84 bpm, about every 2.86 s, and 15% of the film is left to the forest.
prompt.when: Fits nature, outdoor, sustainability and morning-routine films.
prompt.avoid: City or office pictures, and fast edits that fight its calm.

name: Distant city at night
line: A far-off city hum and passing traffic under the voice, late at night.

prompt.what: A distant night city sits under the voice in place of music, dipping 10 dB under each line (8 dB when confident), so the film feels like a late, quiet hour. Cuts fall on a count of 84 bpm, about every 2.86 s, or 2.4 s at 100 bpm when confident.
prompt.when: Fits night-time products, delivery and travel, and stories about working late.
prompt.avoid: Bright daytime pictures, and close-up product shots where a city has no place.

name: Strong wind for tension
line: A harsh, gusting wind makes the problem feel cold and exposed.

prompt.what: A strong gusting wind runs under the problem half of the film and cuts away on one frame at the turn, when the product arrives and warmer sound takes over. Cuts fall about every 2.4 s on a count of 100 bpm, and the wind dips 8 dB under each line.
prompt.when: Fits outdoor gear, insurance, security and any before and after story built on a hard problem.
prompt.avoid: Leaving the wind under the product, which makes the product feel cold.

name: Music only, no voice
line: No voice at all: the music carries the film and the words on screen hit the beat.

prompt.what: No voice; the music plays at full level the whole way (it never dips, 0 dB) and every word on screen lands on a beat, here the groove at 120 bpm. Change the picture once a bar (2 s) in a confident film and every two beats (1 s) at hype, and use small effects only where something on screen makes a sound.
prompt.when: Fits feed ads watched with or without sound, showreels, kinetic type and launch reels.
prompt.avoid: Long sentences on screen, which cannot be read in one beat, and dense effects that bury the music.

name: Loops without a seam
line: The film has no ending: the last beat flows straight back into the first, so it plays on repeat.

prompt.what: Make the film a whole number of bars long, for example eight bars, 16 s at 120 bpm, and cut once a bar, 2 s, so the last bar runs straight back into the first with no fade, no logo sting and no gap. The music dips 9 dB under any line, and the picture's last frame matches its first so the join cannot be heard or seen.
prompt.when: Fits feed posts and website loops that autoplay on repeat, and interface loops cut to music.
prompt.avoid: A logo end card or a fade at the end, which breaks the loop, and voice lines that run across the join.

name: Ease off for the offer
line: The music drops a level for the last seconds so the offer and the ask can breathe.

prompt.what: Bring the music down one level for the last 6 to 8 s, as the groove does 40.3 s in at 120 bpm, so the offer, price and call to action sit in clear space. Cut once a bar, 2 s, through the ending and dip the music 9 dB under the last line.
prompt.when: Fits ads and promos that end on a price, a code or a sign-up.
prompt.avoid: Ending the film at full energy over small text nobody can read.

name: Music at the edges, voice alone between
line: Music opens and closes the film, and the voice has the middle to itself.

prompt.what: The music plays under the first 3 s, fades out over 2 s as the first line starts, and the voice carries the middle on clean room tone; the music comes back on a bar start for the last 4 s and fades again under the logo, as the steady pulse does at 120 bpm. Cuts in the music parts land once a bar, 2 s, and the music dips 9 dB under any line it shares.
prompt.when: Fits demos and explainers with a lot to say, where music all the way through would crowd the voice.
prompt.avoid: Bringing the music back for one line in the middle, and a fade shorter than 1.5 s, which sounds like a mistake.

name: The product plays the beat
line: No music: the clicks, ticks and pops of the product fall into a rhythm and become the beat.

prompt.what: Leave out music and place every click, tick and pop on a 120 bpm grid, one per beat, 0.5 s apart, so the product's own sounds form a beat; on-screen actions are timed to that grid, not the other way round. Effects dip 9 dB under a line, and the beat rests for one beat before each new section so it breathes, about 8% of the film.
prompt.when: Fits product demos and motion pieces with many small actions, and brands that want to sound inventive.
prompt.avoid: Long voice-overs, which fight the rhythm, and actions slowed or rushed just to hit a beat.

name: Build, cut dead, then the line
line: A tense build stops dead, and the most important line plays in the silence.

prompt.what: Run a 2 s pulsing build into the key moment and stop everything on one frame, music and effects, then leave 0.5 s of silence before the most important line plays alone. Music returns one bar later, at 110 bpm (128 at hype), and dips 9 dB under the lines that follow (6 dB at hype).
prompt.when: Fits the one line that sells the film: a price, a promise, a name.
prompt.avoid: Doing it more than once per film, and silences longer than 0.8 s, which feel like a fault.

name: No music, just real sounds
line: No music: only the true sounds of the things on screen, a cup, a box, a pour.

prompt.what: Leave out music and build the soundtrack only from the true sounds of what is on screen, each placed on the frame of contact, like a cup set on a table. Sounds come about once a bar on a count of 84 bpm, every 2.86 s (2.4 s at 100 bpm when confident), and dip 9 dB under a line (8 dB when confident).
prompt.when: Fits food, drink, craft and physical products where the real sound sells, and quiet social clips.
prompt.avoid: Sounds for things the viewer cannot see, and filling every gap; the pauses are part of it.

name: Soft air whoosh
line: A light breath of air on each scene change, barely there.

prompt.what: One soft, airy whoosh on every scene change, started 0.28 s before the cut so its gentle peak sits on the cut frame. Cuts fall on a 90 bpm grid (110 bpm when confident), and each whoosh dips 12 dB (9 dB when confident) under a spoken line, like the music.
prompt.when: Fits calm demos and explainers where changes should feel smooth, not announced.
prompt.avoid: A whoosh on small moves inside a scene, and louder whooshes mixed into the same film.

name: Bright sliding whoosh
line: A clean, bright rush of air as a new screen slides into place.

prompt.what: A bright, airy whoosh for screens and panels sliding in, started 0.5 s ahead so its peak lands on the frame the panel settles. Cuts sit on a 110 bpm grid, and the whoosh dips 9 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits modern product films where screens slide, push and open wide.
prompt.avoid: Using it on hard cuts with no movement, where the air has nothing to follow.

name: Quick pass-by
line: A short, tight whoosh as something flies through the frame.

prompt.what: A short, tight pass-by whoosh for panels flying in and out, started 0.23 s before the move's fastest frame. Cuts fall on a 110 bpm grid (128 bpm at hype), at most one pass-by per cut, and it dips 9 dB (6 dB at hype) under a line.
prompt.when: Fits snappy promos and quick feature montages.
prompt.avoid: Slow moves, where a fast sound feels late, and two pass-bys closer than 0.3 s.

name: Whip pan swish
line: A sharp crack of air as the camera whips to the next shot.

prompt.what: A sharp, very short swish on every whip pan, peaking 0.06 s after it starts, so trigger it two frames before the blur's middle. Cuts fall on a 128 bpm grid and the swish dips 6 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits fast social edits, sports and energetic product montages built on whip pans.
prompt.avoid: More than one whip every two seconds, which turns into noise.

name: Deep whoosh between chapters
line: A big, dark rush of air that marks a new part of the story.

prompt.what: A deep, heavy whoosh only at chapter changes, started 0.84 s early so its low peak lands on the new title or scene. Use two or three in a film, on a 110 bpm grid (128 bpm at hype), dipping 9 dB (6 dB at hype) under a line.
prompt.when: Fits launch films and brand stories with clear chapters.
prompt.avoid: Every cut, which makes the film feel heavy, and calm films.

name: Slow drifting dissolve
line: A long, gentle wash of air under a slow fade between two scenes.

prompt.what: A slow, wide whoosh under each dissolve or slow push, starting 0.93 s before the midpoint of the dissolve so its swell sits in the middle. Changes come on a 90 bpm grid, it dips 12 dB under a line, and 14% of the film is quiet.
prompt.when: Fits calm brand films, wellness and slow, considered reveals.
prompt.avoid: Hard cuts, and stacking it under fast motion.

name: Whistling zip
line: A thin, whistling zip as a small icon or pointer darts across.

prompt.what: A high, whistling zip for a small thing flying past close by, an icon, a pointer or a sticker, started 0.36 s before it crosses the centre. Moves sit on a 110 bpm grid, and the zip dips 9 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits playful product films and animated explainers with small flying elements.
prompt.avoid: Large objects, which need a deeper sound, and premium brands.

name: Fluttering flip
line: A quick flapping flutter as a card or page flips over.

prompt.what: A rhythmic flutter for cards, pages or tiles flipping over, started 0.48 s before the flip is edge-on. Flips fall on a 110 bpm grid, and the flutter dips 9 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits card-flip reveals, stat cards and paper-look films.
prompt.avoid: Flat slides with no turn, and more than one flip on screen at once.

name: Whoosh into a punch
line: A rush of air that ends in a hard punch as the next shot slams in.

prompt.what: A whoosh that ends on a hard punch, started 0.64 s before the cut so the punch lands on the frame the new shot or title slams in. Cuts fall on a 128 bpm grid, at most one punch a bar, dipping 6 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits hype ads and launch films where a title or product slams in.
prompt.avoid: Soft fades, where the hit has nothing to land on, and calm voice-over films.

name: Whoosh into a soft thud
line: A light rush of air that settles on a soft, rounded thud.

prompt.what: A light whoosh that lands on a soft, rounded thud, started 0.54 s before the new scene settles so the thud meets it. Cuts fall on a 110 bpm grid and the sound dips 9 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits confident product films that want weight on scene changes without aggression.
prompt.avoid: Every cut in a long film; keep it for the four or five main changes.

name: Reverse swell into the cut
line: A sound that swells up backwards and stops dead on the new shot.

prompt.what: A reversed swell that grows and stops exactly on the cut, started 1.32 s before the new shot so its sudden stop is the cut. Cuts fall on a 90 bpm grid (110 bpm when confident), and the swell dips 12 dB (9 dB when confident) under a line.
prompt.when: Fits title cards, premium reveals and the turn in a story.
prompt.avoid: Using it on more than three cuts, and fast films where 1.3 s of run-up does not fit.

name: Reverse swell into a hit
line: A backwards swell that sucks in and lands on a hit as the title appears.

prompt.what: A reversed swell that sucks in and lands on a hit, started 1.06 s before the title or product appears so the hit meets its first full frame. Cuts sit on a 110 bpm grid (128 bpm at hype) and the sound dips 9 dB (6 dB at hype) under a line.
prompt.when: Fits dramatic titles, the hook's first word and product reveals.
prompt.avoid: Stacking it with a riser on the same moment; one run-up is enough.

name: Sucked into the next shot
line: A fast inward rush, as if the camera is pulled through the screen.

prompt.what: A short inward rush for zoom-throughs, started 0.64 s before the cut so it peaks as the camera passes through. Cuts fall on a 128 bpm grid and the rush dips 6 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits zoom-through cuts into a screen, a word or an object.
prompt.avoid: Side-to-side moves, which want a pass-by, not an inward rush.

name: Tape stop
line: The music grinds to a halt like a tape slowing down, for a comic stop.

prompt.what: Cut the music on the frame the tape-stop sound starts; the sound itself carries the slowing, falling halt over 1.6 s, so start it 1.6 s before the frame where everything freezes. Hold the frozen picture in silence for half a beat at 110 bpm before the next line, and keep effects 9 dB under that line.
prompt.when: Fits a joke, a wrong turn in the story, or the "but wait" before the fix.
prompt.avoid: Serious brands, and using it more than once per film.

name: Spinning flip
line: A whirling whoosh as a card or logo spins round to its other side.

prompt.what: A whirling, rhythmic whoosh for spins and turns, started 0.63 s before the spin settles so its peak lands as the new face comes round. Spins fall on a 110 bpm grid and dip 9 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits card turns, coin flips and logo spins.
prompt.avoid: Flat slides with no rotation, and more than two spins in a film.

name: Paper slide
line: A soft paper drag as a card or panel slides across.

prompt.what: A soft paper swish for cards and panels sliding across, started 0.21 s before the slide's fastest frame. Slides fall on a 90 bpm grid, dip 12 dB under a line, and 14% of the film is quiet.
prompt.when: Fits paper-look explainers, lists and calm panel moves.
prompt.avoid: Digital, glassy pictures, where paper sounds out of place.

name: Soft cloth swish
line: A brush of fabric as the picture moves, warm and human.

prompt.what: A soft brush of fabric on each move or cut, started 0.15 s before the movement peaks, so it feels like a sleeve passing the lens. Cuts fall on a 90 bpm grid (110 bpm when confident) and the swish dips 12 dB (9 dB when confident) under a line.
prompt.when: Fits fashion, lifestyle and people-led films.
prompt.avoid: Screen-only films, and loud music that hides it.

name: Quick hand swish
line: A bright little swish of a hand as an element snaps into place.

prompt.what: A short, bright hand swish as elements snap into place or a screen swipes over, started 0.14 s before the snap. Snaps fall on a 110 bpm grid and dip 9 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits product films with snappy layout changes and swipes between screens.
prompt.avoid: Slow moves, and big scene changes, which need a fuller whoosh.

name: Page turn between chapters
line: A single page turning as the film moves to its next part.

prompt.what: One real page turn at each chapter change, started 0.19 s before the new chapter's first frame so the paper's peak meets it. Chapters fall on a 90 bpm grid, the turn dips 12 dB under a line, and 14% of the film is quiet.
prompt.when: Fits tutorials, guides, books and story-led explainers with chapters.
prompt.avoid: Turning pages on every cut, and films with no paper or book feel.

name: Gentle swell into a new section
line: A soft rising swell lifts the film into its next part.

prompt.what: A smooth, soft swell that rises and fades into the next section, started 2.2 s before it so its top meets the first frame. Sections fall on a 90 bpm grid (110 bpm when confident) and the swell dips 12 dB (9 dB when confident) under a line.
prompt.when: Fits calm and confident films moving from problem to product, or into a headline.
prompt.avoid: Ending it on a hit, which belongs to louder films, and more than two swells in a film.

name: Pulsing build before the reveal
line: A tense, pulsing build that speeds up for 4 s before the product appears.

prompt.what: A pulsing build that quickens over 4 s and cuts at its loudest, started 3.8 s before the reveal so its peak meets the product's first frame. The film cuts on a 110 bpm grid (128 bpm at hype) under it, and the build dips 9 dB (6 dB at hype) under a line.
prompt.when: Fits launch reveals and teasers that make the viewer wait for the product.
prompt.avoid: Spending it on anything but the main reveal, and voice lines during the last second.

name: Short airy uplift
line: A quick rising rush of air that lifts into the next cut.

prompt.what: A short, bright rising sweep into a cut, started 0.76 s ahead so its top lands on the new shot. Cuts fall on a 128 bpm grid, with an uplift only into section changes, dipping 6 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits energetic edits that move from hook to body, or body to offer.
prompt.avoid: Every cut, and calm films.

name: Long build under the opening
line: A slow, deep build of about 6 s that carries the opening to its first big moment.

prompt.what: A long, deep build of about 6 s under the opening, started 5.83 s before the first big moment so its top meets the title. Cut on a 110 bpm grid (128 bpm at hype) underneath, quickening in the last 2 s, and dip the build 9 dB (6 dB at hype) under any line.
prompt.when: Fits keynote openers, launch films and title sequences.
prompt.avoid: Films under 15 s, which cannot spare 6 s of build, and a busy voice over it.

name: Rising pitch into the drop
line: A build with a pitch you can hear climbing, into a drop or a logo.

prompt.what: A musical build whose pitch climbs for about 3 s, started 2.87 s before the drop or logo so its top lands there. Cut on a 110 bpm grid underneath, and dip it 9 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits films that end on a logo or move into a music drop.
prompt.avoid: A clash with the music's key; check by ear that the climb sits with the track.

name: Rise into a hit
line: A heavy build that lands on a deep hit at the film's biggest moment.

prompt.what: A heavy rising build that ends on a deep hit, started 1.79 s before the biggest moment so the hit lands on its exact frame. Cut on a 128 bpm grid underneath, use it once, and dip it 6 dB under a line.
prompt.when: Fits the peak of a hype film: the product, the number or the logo slamming in.
prompt.avoid: Calm films, and a second hit within the next two seconds.

name: Energy falls away
line: A falling sound right after the peak, letting the film settle down.

prompt.what: A soft falling sweep right after the peak, peaking 0.12 s after it starts and falling away over about 1.2 s, so start it on the frame after the big moment. The film settles onto a 90 bpm grid (110 bpm when confident) and the sweep dips 12 dB (9 dB when confident) under a line.
prompt.when: Fits the step down from the peak into the offer or the close.
prompt.avoid: Using it before the peak, where it drains the energy too early.

name: Warm logo sting
line: A soft shimmer rises and settles into one warm, confident chord on the logo.

prompt.what: A 2.4 s synth sting: a soft rising shimmer that resolves into one warm major chord. Start it 0.86 s before the logo locks, so the warm chord lands on the lock frame; the last cut sits on a bar of the cut grid, 90 bpm (110 bpm when confident), and the music drops 10 dB (8 dB when confident) as the sting begins.
prompt.when: Fits most brand films as a closing signature, the same on every film.
prompt.avoid: Changing the sting from film to film, and talking over it.

name: Open, airy logo sting
line: A wide, floating chord that feels open rather than finished, for a hopeful ending.

prompt.what: A 2.7 s sting whose shimmer settles on an open, unresolved chord that floats instead of closing. Start it 1 s before the logo locks, so the open chord lands on the lock frame; the last cut sits on a bar of the cut grid, 90 bpm (110 bpm when confident), and the music drops 10 dB (8 dB when confident) as the sting begins.
prompt.when: Fits films that end on a question, a teaser or an invitation to find out more.
prompt.avoid: Hard-selling endings with a price, which want a chord that closes.

name: Low, bold logo sting
line: A low, bold chord with weight underneath, for a strong, serious brand.

prompt.what: A 2.1 s sting that rises quickly into a low, bold open fifth with real weight in the bass. Start it 0.76 s before the logo locks, so the low chord lands on the lock frame; the last cut sits on a bar of the cut grid, 110 bpm (128 bpm at hype), and the music drops 8 dB (6 dB at hype) as the sting begins.
prompt.when: Fits security, finance, automotive and serious technology brands.
prompt.avoid: Light, playful brands, and phone-only mixes where the low end disappears.

name: Bright, celebratory logo sting
line: A glassy, glittering rise that opens into a bright, rich chord.

prompt.what: A 2.9 s sting with a glassy, glittering rise into a bright, rich chord, the most celebratory of the logo stings. Start it 1.06 s before the logo locks, so the bright chord lands on the lock frame; the last cut sits on a bar of the cut grid, 110 bpm, and the music drops 8 dB as the sting begins.
prompt.when: Fits launches, upgrades, seasonal offers and anything that should feel like good news.
prompt.avoid: Calm or sensitive subjects, and films already full of chimes.

name: Quick two-second sting
line: A fast shimmer that resolves in well under a second, for very short films.

prompt.what: A 1.9 s sting that resolves fast, so it fits the last 2 s of a 6 to 15 s ad. Start it 0.68 s before the logo locks, so its chord lands on the lock frame; the last cut sits on a bar of the cut grid, 110 bpm (128 bpm at hype), and the music drops 8 dB (6 dB at hype) as the sting begins.
prompt.when: Fits bumper ads, short social cuts and end cards with very little time.
prompt.avoid: Long brand films, where a fuller sting gives the ending more room.

name: Glass win sting
line: A short, glassy rising flourish when a goal or milestone is reached.

prompt.what: A 1.3 s glassy flourish whose brightest note arrives 0.4 s in, so start it that much before the goal, badge or result appears. The music drops 8 dB under it, and the next cut waits at least a bar of the 110 bpm grid.
prompt.when: Fits the one result in a demo: a goal reached, a report finished, a streak kept.
prompt.avoid: Using it for small steps, and more than once per film.

name: Level-up step
line: A quick rising run, like going up a level, when a plan is upgraded.

prompt.what: A quick 1.1 s rising run that peaks 0.42 s in, placed so the peak meets the upgrade, unlock or next tier appearing. Hold the new tier for one bar of the 110 bpm (128 bpm at hype) cut after it, with the music 8 dB (6 dB at hype) down for the run.
prompt.when: Fits upgrades, plan changes, unlocked features and progress moments.
prompt.avoid: Serious subjects, and stacking it with the logo sting.

name: Price ding
line: A small, bright ding as the price or the offer appears.

prompt.what: One small glass ding that peaks 0.32 s in, placed so it meets the frame the price, code or discount lands. The music drops 8 dB (6 dB at hype) for the ding and the price holds at least two bars of the cut grid, 110 bpm (128 bpm at hype).
prompt.when: Fits price reveals, sale ends and offer cards.
prompt.avoid: A ding on every number in the film; keep it for the one the viewer must remember.

name: Quiet wooden sting
line: A short, warm wooden tone, calm and brief, to end gently.

prompt.what: A brief 0.45 s wooden tone that peaks 0.25 s in, used as a gentle full stop on the logo or the last result. The music drops 10 dB under it, on a 90 bpm grid, and 14% of the film stays quiet.
prompt.when: Fits wellness, learning and calm apps that should end softly.
prompt.avoid: Hype films, where it disappears under the music.

name: Small hand bell
line: A clear little hand bell that rings once for an arrival.

prompt.what: One ring of a small hand bell, reaching full ring 0.13 s in, on the frame something arrives or opens; let its 2.6 s ring decay under the next shot. The music drops 10 dB (8 dB when confident), on a cut grid of 90 bpm (110 bpm when confident).
prompt.when: Fits shops, cafés, hotels and gentle arrivals or openings.
prompt.avoid: Tech launches, and ringing it more than twice in a film.

name: Service counter bell
line: A ding of the bell on a service counter, as an order comes in.

prompt.what: A service-counter bell that strikes at once, 0.02 s in, placed on the frame a new order, booking or sale appears. The music drops 8 dB under its ring, on a 110 bpm grid.
prompt.when: Fits retail, restaurant, booking and till products.
prompt.avoid: Using it as the logo sting, and more than one ring per order shown.

name: Typewriter bell
line: The ding of a typewriter reaching the end of a line, as a sentence finishes.

prompt.what: A typewriter bell for the end of a line that strikes 0.03 s in, placed on the frame the headline or quote finishes typing, after the last key sound. Under the ding the music sits 10 dB (8 dB when confident) lower, and the next line starts typing one bar later at 90 bpm (110 bpm when confident).
prompt.when: Fits writing tools, editorial brands and quote cards.
prompt.avoid: Modern glassy pictures, where a mechanical bell feels like a costume.

name: Clock chime for a milestone
line: A warm clock chime that marks time passing or a milestone.

prompt.what: One warm clock strike, 0.02 s to full tone, on the frame a date, a year or a milestone lands, its 2.6 s ring carried under the next shot. Let the strike sit alone, the music 10 dB (8 dB when confident) down, and cut to the next date on the following 90 bpm (110 bpm when confident) bar.
prompt.when: Fits anniversaries, timelines, deadlines and "years in business" films.
prompt.avoid: Striking it on every date of a timeline; keep it for the one that matters.

name: Wind chimes shimmer
line: A soft shimmer of wind chimes for a calm, positive moment.

prompt.what: A soft wind-chime shimmer that blooms 0.91 s in, so start it that early before the calm reveal or the end card. The music drops 10 dB under it, on a 90 bpm grid, and 14% of the film is quiet.
prompt.when: Fits wellness, sleep, nature and kind, quiet brand endings.
prompt.avoid: Fast films, and pairing it with a logo sting in the same few seconds.

name: Sparkling chime run
line: A quick, glittering run of little chimes, like a sprinkle of magic.

prompt.what: A light, sparkling run of chimes that starts bright at once (0 s run-up) and glitters for about 1.9 s; place its start on the frame a reveal begins. The music drops 8 dB under it, on a 110 bpm grid.
prompt.when: Fits gifts, beauty, kids, seasonal offers and "and it just works" moments.
prompt.avoid: Serious brands, and using it as a sting on every scene.

name: Deep boom on the logo
line: A huge, low boom the instant the logo lands, like a film trailer.

prompt.what: A deep cinematic boom whose hit is in its first frame (0 s run-up), so start it on the exact frame the logo or title slams in, the film's one hero moment, and let its 2.5 s tail ring out. Everything else steps back under it, the music dropping 8 dB (6 dB at hype), and the last cut lands on a bar of the cut grid, 110 bpm (128 bpm at hype).
prompt.when: Fits launch films, trailers and big reveals.
prompt.avoid: More than one boom per film, and calm voice-led films.

name: Steel lock
line: A bright metallic ring as the final panel or logo locks into place.

prompt.what: A ringing metal hit with its strike in the first frame (0 s run-up), placed on the exact frame a badge, panel or logo locks; its 1.5 s ring carries the hold, so cut nothing for that long. Pull the music 8 dB (6 dB at hype) back on the strike and bring it up on the next 110 bpm (128 bpm at hype) bar.
prompt.when: Fits hardware, security, industrial and engineering brands.
prompt.avoid: Soft or friendly brands, and pairing it with glass chimes.

name: Soft thud on the end card
line: A gentle, low thud as the end card settles, a full stop you feel.

prompt.what: One soft, low thud with its weight in the first frame (0 s run-up), placed on the frame the end card or last number settles. The music drops 10 dB (8 dB when confident) under it, and the last cut lands on a bar of the cut grid, 90 bpm (110 bpm when confident).
prompt.when: Fits calm and confident films that want weight at the end without a melody.
prompt.avoid: Using it under a logo sting as well; pick one.

name: Phone buzz as the opening signature
line: Every film in a series opens on the same phone buzz on a table, before anything else is heard.

prompt.what: The same signature opener on every film in a series: frame one plays a phone buzzing three times on a table, its first pulse at 0 s, with the notification on screen by 0.3 s; music comes in on the third pulse, sitting 8 dB (6 dB at hype) under the buzz until it ends. Cuts after it keep a grid of 110 bpm (128 bpm at hype).
prompt.when: Fits notification hooks, messaging and alert products, and "you have a new..." openers.
prompt.avoid: Using a buzz with no phone or notification on screen.

name: Warm, conversational voice-over
line: A friendly voice that sounds like a person explaining something to a friend.

prompt.what: A warm, relaxed voice-over at about 140 words a minute (150 when confident), smiling but never selling, with a 0.6 s breath between lines (0.4 s when confident). The bed dips 12 dB under it (10 dB when confident); each line is directed as one person talking to one viewer, over a bed of 92.9 bpm.
prompt.when: Fits explainers, onboarding and product stories; until this voice is made in your account, the studio pairs your current voice with the Calm lo-fi bed, which suits it.
prompt.avoid: Reading like an advert, and lines longer than 6 s.

name: Bright, punchy announcer
line: A big, energetic voice that hits every key word, for loud ads.

prompt.what: A bright, high-energy read at about 170 words a minute in short bursts of three to six words, landing each key word on a beat, with only 0.2 s between lines. The music dips just 6 dB under it, so the voice has to cut through by its own energy, riding a 143.1 bpm track.
prompt.when: Fits sales, launches and sports-energy ads; until it is made, the studio uses your current voice over the Driving electronic, flat out track.
prompt.avoid: Shouting, and long sentences that leave no room for the beat.

name: Calm, patient teacher
line: A steady, unhurried voice that walks the viewer through each step.

prompt.what: A clear, level voice at about 130 words a minute that names each step before the screen shows it, then pauses 0.8 s while the action happens, over a gentle 92.9 bpm bed. Any music sits 12 dB under it and 15% of the film is left to the screen and the pause.
prompt.when: Fits tutorials, help films and training; until it is made, the studio pairs your current voice with the Calm lo-fi bed.
prompt.avoid: Sounding bored or slow; patient is not sleepy.

name: On-camera host, bright and polished
line: A confident presenter talking straight to camera, like a good TV host.

prompt.what: A presenter on camera who speaks at about 150 words a minute with energy and clear diction, cut on speech beats every 1.5 to 3 s with 0.4 s of breath left between lines. Their own room sound stays under them at one steady level (0 dB change) so cuts never drop to silence, and cuts keep a loose count of 100 bpm.
prompt.when: Fits product tours, launch updates and explainers with a face; until a presenter is filmed or made, the studio uses Voice alone on room tone with your current voice.
prompt.avoid: Reading off a script in a flat voice, and music under the whole talk.

name: Founder speaking plainly
line: The person behind the company talking simply and honestly, like a letter read aloud.

prompt.what: A founder or team member speaking to camera at about 130 words a minute, unpolished on purpose, keeping a natural 0.6 s pause between thoughts. No music; their room sound stays steady (0 dB change) and 14% of the film holds on them listening or thinking, cut on a slow count of 84 bpm.
prompt.when: Fits mission films, apologies, thank-you notes and launch letters; until it is filmed, the studio uses Voice alone on room tone.
prompt.avoid: Marketing phrases in their mouth, and cutting out every pause.

name: Two people talking
line: A short, natural exchange between two people, as if overheard.

prompt.what: Two distinct voices in a short exchange, each line under 4 s, with replies coming 0.3 s after the last word (0.2 s when confident) so it sounds like real talk. Any background dips 9 dB under them (8 dB when confident), and each voice sits slightly to the side of its speaker; cuts keep a count of 84 bpm (100 when confident).
prompt.when: Fits customer moments, sketches, animated stories and problem scenes; until the voices are made, the studio uses No music, just real sounds with one voice.
prompt.avoid: Both voices sounding alike, and scripted lines nobody would say out loud.

name: Creator talking to their phone
line: A chatty, close-up voice like someone filming themselves on a phone.

prompt.what: A close, chatty voice at about 170 words a minute, recorded as if on a phone held at arm's length, with breaths cut so only 0.2 s sits between lines (0.1 s at hype). Music dips 9 dB under it (6 dB at hype) and captions follow every word, cut to a 120 bpm track.
prompt.when: Fits creator-style ads, reviews and reaction clips; until it is made, the studio uses your current voice over the Upbeat groove.
prompt.avoid: A studio-perfect sound, which gives the style away, and scripted ad phrases.

name: Deep trailer voice
line: A low, slow, dramatic voice with big pauses, like a film trailer.

prompt.what: A deep, slow voice at about 110 words a minute in short lines of two to five words, each followed by 0.8 s of space (0.5 s at hype) for the music to answer. The music dips 9 dB under each line (6 dB at hype) and swells in every gap, on a 100.1 bpm track.
prompt.when: Fits big launches and teasers; until it is made, the studio uses your current voice over Quiet build, reveal on the drop.
prompt.avoid: Everyday products, where it sounds like a joke, and lines over three seconds.

name: Dry, precise explainer
line: A crisp, plain-spoken voice that says exactly what the product does, no fluff.

prompt.what: A crisp, even voice at about 160 words a minute that states facts plainly, with 0.3 s between lines and no upward lilt at the ends. The bed dips 9 dB under it, and every claim it makes is shown on screen within 1 s, over a 120 bpm pulse.
prompt.when: Fits developer tools, data and B2B products for a technical audience; until it is made, the studio uses your current voice over the Steady pulse for demos.
prompt.avoid: Jokes and hype words, and sounding robotic; dry still means human.

name: Friendly cartoon character
line: A bright, playful character voice for an animated mascot or guide.

prompt.what: A bright, expressive character voice at about 150 words a minute with clear ups and downs, 0.4 s between lines so the animation can react. The music dips 9 dB under it, and mouth movements are timed to the recorded line, never the other way round, over a 120 bpm bed.
prompt.when: Fits mascots, kids and learning films and playful product guides; until it is made, the studio uses your current voice over the Playful chiptune.
prompt.avoid: Copying a known cartoon voice, and a squeaky pitch that tires the ear after 20 s.
